inputs.original_text: In Palakkad on March 28, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan called allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption over the proposed Cooperative Department software project “political.” But calling scrutiny political doesn’t answer the public’s questions. Cooperative members and ordinary people deserve transparency over how their money and essential systems are managed, regardless of who is making the accusations. That means clear disclosure and accountability, not a political contest that leaves the people most affected in the dark.
inputs.modified_text: In Palakkad on March 28, Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan dismissed allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption over the proposed Cooperative Department software project as “political.” That may be true of the accusations, but it is no substitute for answering them. Cooperative members and ordinary people should not bear the cost of opaque decisions about systems and money they depend on. The government owes them clear disclosure and accountability; treating scrutiny as a political fight risks protecting institutions from questions instead of protecting the public.
